content: The sky is blue because sunlight is scattered by tiny air molecules. Shorter wavelengths—blue and violet—scatter much more strongly than longer wavelengths, so blue light is spread across the sky and reaches our eyes from all directions. Near sunrise or sunset, light travels through more atmosphere, so the blue is scattered away and red/orange tones dominate.
